Manage a receiving region as displacement pressure rises. Whether that pressure becomes a crisis or a manageable transition comes down to how well the region prepared.

Institutional preparedness, not the scale of arrivals alone, is what determines outcomes. Uganda's refugee policy — granting land access and the right to work and move freely, integrated alongside host communities — is widely cited by policy researchers as a model of how institutional capacity can turn large-scale displacement into manageable, even mutually beneficial, coexistence.

    Displacement pressure

    i

    Strain isn't just a snapshot — it's how far cumulative arrivals have outrun cumulative capacity over the whole run. Higher strain directly cuts into the region's income each round (service shortfalls and friction cost money), and stays elevated even if you catch up later.

    Capacity planning forecast

    Integration

    i

    Only Integration Services capacity moves people from pending to integrated — housing and infrastructure don't speed this up. Services throughput caps how many people can be integrated per round regardless of how much funding you have, so a backlog of pending arrivals can only clear as fast as services capacity allows.

    Real-world comparison

    Your region has integrated 0% of arrivals so far — still well short of the broad-access standard Uganda's model is cited for, which extends near-universal access to land, work rights, and freedom of movement for arrivals.

    Real-world benchmark: as of 2023, 89% of working-age refugees resettled in the U.S. within the previous five years were employed (Migration Policy Institute) — a genuine, sourced outcome statistic for real resettlement systems, not the same measurement as this game's own broader integration metric (language, employment, and education access combined).     Regional wellbeing

    i

    Wellbeing is the simple average of three separately-tracked scores, not one blended number: service quality reflects strain across the whole run so far, economic health is your funds measured against a fixed reference scale, and social cohesion is the share of everyone who's arrived that's actually been integrated.

    Policy toolkit

    Real-world institutional levers, funded separately from capacity. Each can be strengthened up to three times.

    Streamlined Credentialing

    +15% funds contributed back by integrated people, per level.

    Language-Access Funding

    +15% integration throughput, per level.

    Community Sponsorship

    +6 effective capacity against strain, per level.

    Neighbouring district

    i

    A second region with a different starting profile: plenty of housing, no integration services, little money and a higher background pressure. It runs alongside yours every round with its own funds and its own investments. When your region is calm and holds a cushion of funds you can send it support. If you leave it in critical strain, extra people reach your region every round.
